hit_points.formula_note: At Ninja levels, gain 6 HP + Constitution modifier per level.

design_identity.combat_style: Switches between Throwing, Shadow Arts, and Ninpou to pressure priority targets, control movement, punish vulnerable enemies, and adapt to enemy defenses.

branch_fantasies.throwing_mastery: Physical pressure branch. Uses Bleeding, Reeling, Hamstrung, Maimed, and execution sequencing to disable or isolate targets.
branch_fantasies.shadow_arts: Mobility and assassination branch. Uses teleportation, repositioning, evasive tempo, and isolated-target payoffs.
branch_fantasies.ninpou_training: Elemental casting branch. Uses bolts, fields, and bursts for ranged magical damage and spatial control.

strengths: Has both physical and magical threat profiles
Can pivot between poke, setup, control, and execution
Throwing can punish high-magic-resistance enemies without feeling like a fallback
weaknesses: Needs sequencing and stance management to maximize value
Durability remains modest in direct attrition
Several premium effects depend on prior setup or conditioned targets
Final Strike is powerful but committal

ninja_stances.description: The Ninja uses three combat stances. Only one stance may be active at a time.

throwing_condition_model.description: Throwing is a full branch, not a fallback. It mirrors Ninpou's single-target / control / burst structure, but expresses power through physical conditions instead of elemental spell damage.

soul_system.description: Soul is the central concentration buff of the class. It amplifies every branch and makes setup-to-payoff turns more explosive.

core_design_rules: Ninja begins at character level 2 because level 1 belongs to Novice.
Ninja uses character-level scaling, not subclass-level scaling.
The main scaling baselines are acquisition level plus major upgrades at character levels 5 and 9 where applicable.
Throwing Mastery, Shadow Arts, and Ninpou Training are stances that enhance branches rather than hard-locking access to them.
The first stance change each turn is free and exists to encourage adaptation rather than punish flexibility.
Throwing is a full branch with its own single-target skill, control field, and burst skill.
Throwing should outperform Ninpou against conditioned or magic-resistant targets, while Ninpou should remain better at raw elemental area pressure and spell-based ranged damage.
Shadow Arts should remain the tempo and mobility branch, not the branch with the highest raw ranged damage.
Soul must meaningfully support Throwing, Shadow Arts, Ninpou, and Final Strike.
Final Strike is intentionally high-commitment and should feel dangerous to use.
